content: Polyethylene glycol is a laxative approved by the FDA for the treatment of constipation. It is commonly associated with adverse reactions such as diarrhea, flatulence, nausea, and stomach cramps. Adult Indications and Dosage Indications: Polyethylene glycol is used to relieve occasional constipation (irregularity) and generally produces a bowel movement within 1 to 3 days. Directions: Do not exceed the recommended dosage unless directed by a physician. The provided scoop is designed to measure 17 grams of powder when filled to the top (level scoop). Adults and children aged 17 years and older should: Fill the scoop completely with the product to obtain the correct dose (17 grams). Level the scoop with a knife or flat object. Stir and dissolve the powder in 4 to 8 ounces of any beverage (cold, hot, or room temperature) and drink. Use once daily and for no more than 7 days. For children aged 16 years or younger, consult a doctor. Off-Label Use and Dosage (Adult) There is limited information available regarding off-label guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported use of polyethylene glycol in adult patients. Pediatric Indications and Dosage FDA-Labeled Indications and Dosage: The safety and effectiveness of polyethylene glycol have not been established in children. Off-Label Use and Dosage: There is limited information regarding off-label guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported use of polyethylene glycol in pediatric patients. Contraindications There is limited information regarding contraindications for polyethylene glycol in the drug label. Warnings Allergy Alert: Do not use if allergic to polyethylene glycol. Do Not Use: If you have kidney disease, unless advised and supervised by a doctor. Consult a Doctor Before Use If You Have: Nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain. A sudden change in bowel habits lasting more than 2 weeks. Irritable bowel syndrome. Consult a Doctor or Pharmacist Before Use If You Are: Taking a prescription drug. When Using This Product: Loose, watery, or more frequent stools may occur. Stop Use and Consult a Doctor If: You experience rectal bleeding or worsening nausea, bloating, cramping, or abdominal pain, as these may indicate a serious condition. You develop diarrhea. You need to use a laxative for longer than 1 week. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Consult a healthcare professional before use. Keep Out of Reach of Children: In case of overdose, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately (1-800-222-1222). Adverse Reactions Clinical Trials Experience: Limited information is available regarding clinical trial data for polyethylene glycol. Postmarketing Experience: Reported adverse reactions include diarrhea, flatulence, nausea, and stomach cramps. Drug Interactions Limited information is available regarding drug interactions with polyethylene glycol. Use in Specific Populations Pregnancy: If pregnant or breastfeeding, consult a healthcare professional before use. There is no Australian Drug Evaluation Committee (ADEC) guidance on its use during pregnancy. Labor and Delivery: No FDA guidance is available on its use during labor and delivery. Nursing Mothers: Consult a healthcare professional before use. Pediatric Use: Safety and effectiveness have not been established in children. Geriatric Use: No FDA guidance is available for geriatric patients. Gender: No FDA guidance is available for specific gender populations. Race: No FDA guidance is available for specific racial populations. Renal Impairment: No FDA guidance is available for patients with renal impairment. Hepatic Impairment: No FDA guidance is available for patients with hepatic impairment. Females of Reproductive Potential and Males: No FDA guidance is available for these populations. Immunocompromised Patients: No FDA guidance is available for immunocompromised patients. Administration and Monitoring Administration: Polyethylene glycol is administered orally. Monitoring: Limited information is available regarding monitoring requirements for polyethylene glycol. IV Compatibility Limited information is available regarding IV compatibility of polyethylene glycol. Overdosage In case of overdose, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately (1-800-222-1222). Pharmacology Mechanism of Action: Polyethylene glycol works as an osmotic laxative. Structure: Each dose contains 17 grams of polyethylene glycol 3350 (in each level scoop). Pharmacodynamics and Pharmacokinetics: Limited information is available regarding the pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics of polyethylene glycol. Nonclinical Toxicology: Limited information is available regarding nonclinical toxicology. Clinical Studies Limited information is available regarding clinical studies of polyethylene glycol. Storage Store at 20°-25°C (68°-77°F). Do not use if the printed foil seal under the cap is missing, open, or broken. Alcohol Interaction The interaction between alcohol and polyethylene glycol has not been established. Consult your doctor regarding the effects of consuming alcohol while using this medication.
